details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/persist_orchestrator.py:727-751 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The `_superseded` helper in `classify_check_runs` lets any newer run with the same name hide a cancelled run. It does not apply the CI-check-name exception from `PR_CHECKS_JQ_SUPERSEDE_DEFS` in scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh, which requires the same Actions run id from `details_url` when the name is `AUTO_MERGE_REQUIRED_CI_CHECK` (default `lint`).
  WHY: A cancelled CI `lint` run can be hidden by a newer `lint` run from another workflow (lint-pr-body-auto-close.yml or lint-plan-archival.yml). The wave check then reports `green` while the final-merge gate (`_mark_superseded --arg ci`) still blocks the same head. All four reviewers rate this MAJOR. The line references differ (luna 727-732, gemini 746-751; sonnet and minimax give the symbol only), and they are merged here as the same `_superseded` helper.
- scripts/persist_orchestrator.py:761-777 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: In the `classify_check_runs` outcome ladder, a truncated check-runs page whose runs are all `skipped` or `neutral` leaves `kept` empty. The `elif kept and result["truncated"]` guard never fires, so the outcome is `no_checks` instead of `pending`.
  WHY: After `PERSIST_ORCH_WAVE_CHECK_MAX_WAIT_MINUTES` the result becomes `no_checks_timeout`. The poller then clears the wait and fails open: a failing check on a page it never read is ignored and the judge is skipped. This contradicts the documented rule "a truncated page ... is never green". Severity disagreement: sonnet rates it NIT; gemini, minimax, luna and glm rate it MAJOR, so the highest (MAJOR) is used.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:20240-20243 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The poller's handling of the classifier result misreads an empty `kept` set on a truncated input whose runs are all ignored. It ends at `no_checks` instead of `pending`.
  WHY: The poller then fails open. This is the poller side of the truncated-page finding above; luna's entry for that finding also cites orchestrate_poll_process.sh:20152, 20240-20242.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:persist_orch_wave_check (restamp branch `elif [ "${pwc_wait_head}" != "${pwc_sha}" ]`) | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: The wait clock restarts every time the integration PR head differs from `wave_check_wait_head`, and nothing limits the restarts. While the head keeps moving, `waited_minutes` never reaches `PERSIST_ORCH_WAVE_CHECK_MAX_WAIT_MINUTES`.
  WHY: The outcome stays `pending` (hold) and never becomes `timeout`. That defeats the plan's cap (docs/plans/persistent-unattended-workflows-plan.md line 537), and each restart posts a state comment.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:20087-20092, 20122-20129, 20237, 31648-31651 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: A red or timeout outcome calls `_persist_orch_wave_check_clear`, which deletes `wave_check_wait_since` and `wave_check_wait_head`. The next tick then takes the `boundary_first_seen` hold path instead of reaching the judge.
  WHY: A persistent red check reaches the judge only every other tick, and each cycle makes two extra `post_state_comment` writes. This contradicts the agents.d/8427-p9-persist-wave-check.md "Failure modes" text "re-invokes the judge each tick". All four reviewers rate this NIT. The line references differ (gemini 20087-20092; luna 20122-20129, 20237, 31648-31651).
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:20087-20092 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: When the head has moved, the restamp `_persist_orch_wave_check_stamp "${pwc_sha}"` posts the state comment before classification. A green, red or timeout result then posts it again through `_persist_orch_wave_check_clear` in the same tick.
  WHY: Each such tick makes one redundant GitHub comment write against the shared API budget (section 14).
- scripts/persist_orchestrator.py:835-865 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The fenced judge block renders untrusted data (log tails, check names) without making sure that fence-closing strings such as `=== END UNTRUSTED WAVE CHECK ===` are not embedded in it.
  WHY: Malformed or hostile data could close the fence early or inject prompt-like text. Note: sonnet reports this refuted (`_WAVE_CHECK_EQ_RUN_RE` plus the `UNTRUSTED_DATA: ` prefix), and glm reports the fence contract verified clean by tests/test_workflow_untrusted_input_contract.py:980-1003.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:20146-20147 | severity=low | confidence=HIGH
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: A `mktemp` failure logs `outcome=error reason=scratch_unwritable`, and then `_persist_orch_wave_check_clear scratch_unwritable` logs a second line, `outcome=cleared reason=scratch_unwritable`.
  WHY: The double log line is redundant because the wait fields were never set on this path. It is consistent with the contract, since both tokens are registered.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "Any failure: set INVOKE_JUDGE_FOR_STUCK=true so the existing judge path runs."
  expected_change_site: scripts/persist_orchestrator.py, classify_check_runs; scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh, the wave-check invocation
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: The classifier counts a completed failure only when its name is in `--required-names` (persist_orchestrator.py lines 741-744), and the poller passes `ORCH_FINAL_MERGE_REQUIRED_CHECKS`, so a failed check outside that list yields `green` and the judge never runs. glm notes that the shipped fragment and changelog (agents.d/8427-p9-persist-wave-check.md:7, changelog.d/8427-p9-persist-wave-check.md) document this narrowing on purpose, so either the issue text or the docs are wrong. sonnet dropped this as a deliberate design choice that matches the final-merge gate (pr_checks_lib.sh line 186, orchestrate_poll_process.sh line 3076).
- requirement: "Any pending: do not advance this tick."
  expected_change_site: scripts/persist_orchestrator.py, `_wave_check_required` and `classify_check_runs`
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: When `ORCH_FINAL_MERGE_REQUIRED_CHECKS` is explicitly empty, `_wave_check_required` selects `mode == "none"` and `classify_check_runs` sets `pending` to an empty list, so a run still in progress can produce `green` and the wave advances.
- requirement: The agents fragment convention requires both a `- PREFIX` registry bullet and a `LOG_PREFIX.name=PREFIX` registration line.
  expected_change_site: agents.d/8427-p9-persist-wave-check.md ("Stable log prefixes (contractual)" block)
  confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The fragment adds the `` - `PERSIST` wave_check component (#8427 P9) `` bullet but no `LOG_PREFIX.name=PERSIST_WAVE_CHECK` line, which the reviewers say sibling fragments (including P8) carry. sonnet and glm report this refuted: sibling P3-P8 fragments have no such line, and `LOG_PREFIX.name=PERSIST` is already registered in agents.d/8428-persist-attempt-journal.md:15-16.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/persist_orchestrator.py:classify_check_runs, nested helper `_superseded(r)` | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The helper applies only the general supersede rule and leaves out the `PR_CHECKS_JQ_SUPERSEDE_DEFS` CI-name exception (scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh lines 97-125; `_pr_auto_merge_required_ci_check_name` lines 588-602 resolves the name to `lint`). Any newer run with the same name hides a cancelled run.
  WHY: A cancelled CI `lint` is hidden by a later `lint` from another workflow, giving `green` and advancing the wave, while the final-merge gate (`_mark_superseded` with `--arg ci`, pr_checks_lib.sh lines 347/373) still blocks the same head. Suggested fix: pass the CI name and require the same `/actions/runs/<id>` in `details_url`.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:persist_orch_wave_check, restamp branch `elif [ "${pwc_wait_head}" != "${pwc_sha}" ]` | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The wait clock restarts on every head move, with no limit, so `waited_minutes` never reaches `PERSIST_ORCH_WAVE_CHECK_MAX_WAIT_MINUTES`.
  WHY: The boundary is held indefinitely (pending, never timeout), against plan line 537, and each restart posts a state comment. Suggested fix: keep the original `wave_check_wait_since`, or add a second total-wait field that is never reset.
- scripts/persist_orchestrator.py:classify_check_runs, `elif kept and result["truncated"]` / `else: result["outcome"] = "no_checks"` | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: A truncated page whose runs are all skipped or neutral gives `no_checks`, which becomes `no_checks_timeout` and leads to a skip.
  WHY: A failing check on an unread page is ignored (fail open). Suggested fix: `elif result["truncated"]: result["outcome"] = "pending"` before the `kept` branches.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:persist_orch_wave_check, `red|timeout)` branch calling `_persist_orch_wave_check_clear` plus the `boundary_first_seen` block | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Clearing on red makes the next tick stamp and hold without calling the judge.
  WHY: The judge runs only every other tick, with two extra `post_state_comment` writes per cycle, and the fragment's "re-invokes the judge each tick" is now wrong. Suggested fix: restamp instead of clearing, or correct the fragment.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:persist_orch_wave_check, restamp followed by `_persist_orch_wave_check_clear` | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: A head move makes the restamp post the state comment, and the clear helper posts it again in the same tick.
  WHY: One redundant comment write per such tick against the API budget. Suggested fix: update `pwc_wait` in memory and stamp only in `pending|no_checks`.
- NOTE: Pass-1 items checked and dropped (3 related items): minimax's missing `LOG_PREFIX.name` (sibling fragments have no such line); gpt-6-luna's required-names narrowing (a design choice matching pr_checks_lib.sh line 186 and orchestrate_poll_process.sh line 3076); gemini's fence-closing strings (`_WAVE_CHECK_EQ_RUN_RE` plus the `UNTRUSTED_DATA: ` prefix; covered by tests).
- HARDENING_SUGGESTIONS (2 related items): a truncated check before `elif kept:` (2 lines); a `--ci-check-name` argument with a same-run-id rule in `_superseded` (8-10 lines). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 3
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
